title: Why Victor did not follow up; Zutty and Cliff Jackson
summary: Wonder why Victor did no more sessions, Zutty Singleton on the sides, and Zutty's opinion of Cliff Jackson as pianist.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, it's a wonder to me that Moore wasn't done to follow up those two Victor sessions because...

Well, yes, it was, I wonder, but they had other artists there. I think they had Count Basie and some others tied up with them. Well, those records made a hit and got acclaim anywhere they were heard, you know. George Haver wrote them up very enthusiastically, you know. And down there. Yeah.
I said, Zutti, Zutti was on those sides, you know.
Yeah, she was on those sides, that's right.

I was talking to Zutti, but Jettirold, he's, you know, he's putting down Cliff a little bit up there one night, but... He says he, he, all boys just can't play piano. And, like, you know, said, Jettirold, he can play, and he mentioned some other people, and... But Zutti didn't, I mean, you know, he gets along with them all right, and thinks Cliff's a good businessman, and he is. But he don't think much of him as a temp piano player, really.
Zutti's singing. Talking about Cliff Jackson. Oh, I see.
